recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-3774; future clinical-document confidentiality constraints should follow the later Bundle.meta.security direction or be handled by specific active profiles, not by restoring the removed base Composition element.
issue_request: FHIR-3774 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification Structured Documents change request against DSTU1 Composition. It asked to make Composition.confidentiality optional because confidentiality is not relevant for all Composition use cases, while allowing clinical-document profiles to require it where appropriate.
initial_application: The Jira comments record svn revision 4661. In the git mirror, that revision is c252f36517f7c77524bde4f19390d450b001f167; before/after source checks show the old source/composition/composition-spreadsheet.xml row for Composition.confidentiality changed from 1..1 to 0..1. The same revision also handled nearby FHIR-3775 clinical-document profile and subject work, explaining why the commit subject does not name FHIR-3774.
additional_context: Composition remains active in the current build, but later Structured Documents issue FHIR-17301 removed Composition.confidentiality entirely for R5 because it duplicated security-tag functionality. That later issue is already represented on the combined branch by 3f1e99663a2dd3eaaa0ad9b8349b76af6602842f. Current Composition source has no active Composition.confidentiality element or search parameter, the CDA note maps ClinicalDocument.confidentialityCode to Bundle.meta.security, and the $document operation tells servers to determine a document Bundle.meta.security high-water mark. The legacy source/profiles/cda.profile.xml profile still contains a required Composition.confidentiality entry, but source/fhir.ini comments that profile out, so it is not a current build input.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The seed requirement that base Composition not require confidentiality is satisfied because current active source no longer defines the element and later approved guidance uses Bundle.meta.security rather than reintroducing a required Composition.confidentiality field.
